facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: On the same unadjusted basis, debt to EBITDA improved from 10.32x in FY2024 to 4.95x in FY2025, and interest cover was 2.94x over the last twelve months. Liquidity of USD 1,409.5 million is almost all undrawn revolver, against USD 277.0 million of debt due within a year, including USD 250.0 million of notes maturing December 15, 2026. Annual and quarterly figures sit on different Hawthorne perimeters, and the covenant earnings definition is not reconciled in the filings. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Unadjusted total debt to EBITDA improved from 10.32x in FY2024 to 4.95x in FY2025 because EBITDA roughly doubled, from USD 215.8 million to USD 425.5 million, while carrying debt fell from USD 2,226.8 million to USD 2,106.4 million. The gain came from a better gross margin rate, up from 23.94% to 30.59% on lower sales, and from smaller impairment, restructuring and other charges, down from USD 146.3 million to USD 83.8 million, not from growth. At June 27, 2026 the ratio is 6.12x on last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 345.3 million, which absorbs the USD 101.8 million loss on selling the Hawthorne business; income from operations on the continuing perimeter rose to USD 549.7 million over nine months from USD 525.7 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103, 123; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3, 12, 19; calculation R1; calculation R2; calculation L1; calculation D1; calculation D2; calculation I1; calculation I2; calculation V1; calculation V4; calculation V7

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The annual figures include Hawthorne in continuing operations while the nine-month and quarterly figures exclude it, so no continuing-operations last-twelve-months series can be built from the filings. This agrees with the source readiness assessment that a continuing-operations series cannot be built; this module therefore uses a consolidated EBITDA that includes discontinued operations, which can be built and is labelled as a different measure. Interim statements are unaudited and seasonal, with more than three quarters of annual sales in the second and third fiscal quarters, so a June balance sheet is not comparable with a September one. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against reading the unadjusted 6.12x as overstated is that interest cover on the same basis is only 2.94x and that free cash flow after dividends was USD 15.8 million for nine months, so internal funding for a USD 250.0 million maturity is thin even without the sale loss. The view would change if fiscal 2026 annual results showed earnings below the level implied by the covenant ratios, or if the receivables purchase programme were not renewed; it would improve if the notes were repaid from revolver capacity with liquidity staying well above the USD 277.0 million of debt due within a year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20, 52, 54; calculation F5; calculation V9; calculation LQ3

facts.text: - Cash conversion is adequate over a full year but leaves little after dividends in the first nine months. Over the last twelve months free cash flow was USD 263.3 million and dividends USD 154.4 million, leaving USD 108.9 million, whereas the nine months to June 27, 2026 left only USD 15.8 million after dividends. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the cautious reading is the record of repayment and the room in the structure: the company prepaid USD 250.0 million and USD 75.0 million of term loan in FY2024 and FY2025, carrying debt fell USD 120.4 million between those year-ends, reported covenant leverage is 3.78x against a 5.00x maximum, revolver loans fell from USD 427.0 million at December 27, 2025 to USD 25.0 million at June 27, 2026 as receivables were collected and sold, availability was USD 979.8 million at its lowest fiscal 2026 quarter-end, and the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 produced USD 131.2 million of free cash flow. The view would improve if the notes are repaid without lifting revolver use above its December 2025 level, if the receivables programme is renewed on similar terms and if the gross margin rate holds above the prior-year level. It would worsen if the notes are repaid mainly from revolver borrowings while the programme lapses, if third-quarter freight costs persist, or if dividends keep exceeding free cash flow before the autumn collection. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Scotts Miracle-Gro is a listed company with no sponsor; a family partnership holds about 23% of the shares, down from 24% a year earlier, and the incoming chief executive, in office from June 26, 2026, is a general partner of that partnership. Substantially all domestic subsidiaries guarantee the credit facilities and the senior notes, but the note guarantees can be released, including when a guarantor is designated an unrestricted subsidiary, so structural support depends on indenture terms that are not supplied. Hawthorne North America was sold on April 8, 2026 for Vireo shares and a warrant, which the company transferred to a consolidated partner-owned vehicle for a promissory note, and an earlier sale of an investment holding company went to a second such vehicle; the company holds call options and the vehicles can put assets back. The credit consequence is that owner behaviour is more predictable than under a sponsor, with no extraction through fees or leveraged recapitalisation seen in the filings, but the dividend of USD 0.66 per share each quarter keeps priority over faster debt paydown. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is recurring in category but not contractual: consumers replenish lawn and garden products each season, yet retailers place orders from late winter and the company reports minimal carryover of open orders, so there is no backlog to underwrite the year. Net sales fell 3.93% in fiscal 2025 with Hawthorne included and rose 2.41% in nine months to June 27, 2026 without it, from volume and mix of 2.0% and pricing of 0.4%, with a favourable mix from branded soils, grass seed, controls and fertiliser offsetting lower mulch sales. Pricing power is limited: two retailers hold 52% of sales, the company states that market conditions may limit its ability to raise prices to offset raw material costs, and private label competes in its markets. The credit implication is that cost inflation is absorbed in margin before it is recovered in price, and that demand is discretionary and exposed to weather and consumer behaviour. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Materials were 50.98% of nine-month cost of sales, manufacturing labor and overhead 23.97% and distribution and warehousing 21.20%, so most cost is variable with volume or input prices rather than fixed. Inputs include urea and other fertiliser, resin, diesel, natural gas, peat, bark and grass seed; the company buys part of its needs ahead of the season and hedges diesel and urea, but imports from China and other countries expose it to tariffs. Selling cost carries operating leverage: advertising and other marketing were USD 196.8 million over nine months, 43.67% of selling, general and administrative cost, after planned increases. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through marketing and incentive pay, but not against a sustained freight or tariff shock, as the 0.9 percentage point fall in the third-quarter gross margin rate shows. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital spending was USD 97.4 million in fiscal 2025, 2.85% of net sales and 1.30x depreciation and amortization, so the business needs modest reinvestment but cannot cut it enough to matter against USD 154.4 million of dividends over twelve months. The main cash swing is working capital: inventory is built in the first quarter, USD 846.7 million at December 27, 2025 against USD 481.4 million at June 27, 2026, and receivables rose USD 552.1 million over the nine months to June 27, 2026 and are collected in the fourth quarter, which is why free cash flow was USD 132.1 million for nine months but USD 263.3 million over twelve months. Cash interest paid was USD 117.4 million over twelve months, while cash taxes paid were only USD 5.6 million over nine months, a benefit from deferred tax assets that the Hawthorne tax loss extends by an amount not stated and that will not last indefinitely. EBITDA therefore converted into free cash flow of 64.37% in fiscal 2025, adequate for debt service but with limited surplus for deleveraging once dividends are paid. Supplier-financed payables of USD 23.7 million at June 27, 2026 are small beside the receivables programme, so that funding source adds little risk. The notes fall due at the seasonal low: on December 27, 2025 balances, liquidity of USD 988.1 million would fall to USD 517.8 million if the programme were not available and the revolver also funded the notes. The spring build then adds receivables and inventory: at March 28, 2026 the programme had removed USD 654.1 million of receivables, and without it and after funding the notes liquidity would have been USD 257.7 million, 22.18% of the reported USD 1,161.8 million, before any earnings shortfall. Leverage then rises from both sides, lower EBITDA and higher revolver debt, moving the reported covenant ratio from 3.78x toward its 5.00x maximum on a definition that cannot be tested here. This is arithmetic on reported balances, not a forecast. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Scotts Miracle-Gro presents an adequate business profile supported by leading brands, a nine-month gross margin rate of 35.67%, up 1.26 percentage points on the prior-year nine months, and a USD 1,500.0 million revolver with availability of at least USD 979.8 million at each fiscal 2026 quarter-end reported, but credit quality is constrained by retailer concentration, a two-quarter earnings season, thin free cash flow after dividends in the first nine months and negative equity. Cash-flow durability appears adequate over a full year, with USD 108.9 million left after dividends over the last twelve months, and weak before the autumn collection. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on revolver availability, the receivables programme and the covenant earnings measure for the 2026 notes, and on market access for the 2029 notes. The primary downside path is a weak spring season with a lapsed receivables programme, which raises revolver use and leverage together. Comparison with sector peers is not established because no peer data is supplied; both rating agencies kept ratings in the single-B category in August 2025. Further analysis would require the fiscal 2026 annual report, the renewal status of the receivables programme, the credit agreement's earnings definition and the proxy statement. The top risk is dependence on revolver capacity and the receivables programme for the spring peak and the December 2026 maturity. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The strongest support is the franchise. Leading brands and the exclusive Roundup agency produced a gross margin rate of 35.67% over nine months, up 1.26 percentage points, which lifts EBITDA and interest cover and lets the company absorb moderate cost increases. The second support is liquidity: availability under the USD 1,500.0 million revolver was USD 979.8 million at the lowest fiscal 2026 quarter-end reported and USD 1,381.8 million at June 27, 2026, so liquidity covered the USD 250.0 million of notes 3.95x at the low and 5.64x in June. The third is a record of paying debt down, with carrying debt falling USD 120.4 million between FY2024 and FY2025 and a lower interest bill, which gives creditors evidence that cash is applied to debt in good years. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The largest weakness is the funding of the seasonal build. The programme that removed USD 654.1 million of receivables at March 28, 2026 is uncommitted, and without it liquidity at that date would have been USD 507.7 million rather than USD 1,161.8 million. The second is thin cash after dividends, USD 15.8 million for nine months and USD 108.9 million for twelve months, which leaves little internal funding for the notes. The third is retailer concentration, 52% of fiscal 2025 net sales in two customers, which limits pricing and concentrates risk in the two quarters that earn most of the year. Unadjusted leverage of 6.12x, negative equity, cost exposure to freight and tariffs, and free cash flow that benefits from cash taxes of only USD 5.6 million over nine months complete the weaknesses. ## Request

Source-readiness assessment for Scotts Miracle-Gro Co (issuer smg-825542), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings can support the requested financial, business and credit work, and what remains missing. No credit conclusion is drawn.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The source set supports a consolidated financial and business snapshot of Scotts Miracle-Gro as of June 27, 2026, with limitations, but nothing later, so creditors cannot rely on it for the December 2026 note maturity, covenant terms or market pricing.

The latest filing was signed 105 days before the as-of date and its balance sheet is 144 days old. The USD 250 million of senior notes maturing 2026-12-15 fall 27 days after the as-of date and the sources do not show how they were handled. No executed credit agreement or indenture, no rating after August 2025, no market quote, no peer set and no portfolio is supplied. The 2025 annual report includes the divested Hawthorne business while the 2026 quarterly reports exclude it, so year-on-year and last-twelve-month comparisons need care. Seven material gaps are open and none is critical.

## Request

Financial foundation for Scotts Miracle-Gro Co (issuer smg-825542), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied filings, up to the quarter ended 2026-06-27. No credit recommendation is made.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Scotts Miracle-Gro's unadjusted leverage is 6.12x at June 27, 2026, inflated by a USD 101.8 million sale loss, while covenant leverage of 3.78x sits inside its 5.00x limit, so the nearer creditor questions are refinancing and liquidity.

On the same unadjusted basis, debt to EBITDA improved from 10.32x in FY2024 to 4.95x in FY2025, and interest cover was 2.94x over the last twelve months. Liquidity of USD 1,409.5 million is almost all undrawn revolver, against USD 277.0 million of debt due within a year, including USD 250.0 million of notes maturing December 15, 2026. Annual and quarterly figures sit on different Hawthorne perimeters, and the covenant earnings definition is not reconciled in the filings.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12, 19, 20, 22, 54; 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; calculation L1; calculation V7; calculation V4; calculation V1; calculation V9; calculation LQ3
### Key findings

Unadjusted total debt to EBITDA improved from 10.32x in FY2024 to 4.95x in FY2025 because EBITDA roughly doubled, from USD 215.8 million to USD 425.5 million, while carrying debt fell from USD 2,226.8 million to USD 2,106.4 million. The gain came from a better gross margin rate, up from 23.94% to 30.59% on lower sales, and from smaller impairment, restructuring and other charges, down from USD 146.3 million to USD 83.8 million, not from growth. At June 27, 2026 the ratio is 6.12x on last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 345.3 million, which absorbs the USD 101.8 million loss on selling the Hawthorne business; income from operations on the continuing perimeter rose to USD 549.7 million over nine months from USD 525.7 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103, 123; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3, 12, 19; calculation R1; calculation R2; calculation L1; calculation D1; calculation D2; calculation I1; calculation I2; calculation V1; calculation V4; calculation V7

Unadjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 1.37x in FY2024, 3.24x in FY2025 and 2.94x over the last twelve months, as cash interest paid fell from USD 157.7 million to USD 131.4 million and then to USD 117.4 million on a last-twelve-months basis. The issuer's own coverage ratio is 5.67x against a 3.00x minimum for fiscal 2026, but it uses an adjusted earnings measure that the filings do not reconcile, so the two ratios cannot be compared directly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103, 118; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 20; calculation L2; calculation V3; calculation V6; calculation V9

Operating cash flow was USD 195.2 million for the nine months to June 27, 2026 against USD 197.2 million a year earlier, after a USD 552.1 million seasonal build in receivables. Capital spending of USD 63.1 million left free cash flow of USD 132.1 million, and dividends of USD 116.3 million took most of it, leaving USD 15.8 million. Lower sales of receivables under an uncommitted purchase programme reduced operating cash flow, so the cushion above dividends depends on that programme and on working-capital timing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 51, 52; calculation F4; calculation F5

Liquidity at June 27, 2026 was USD 1,409.5 million, made up of USD 27.7 million of cash and USD 1,381.8 million of revolver availability after USD 93.2 million of letters of credit and USD 25.0 million drawn. Debt due within twelve months was USD 277.0 million, of which USD 250.0 million is the senior notes maturing December 15, 2026. The filing says the company intends to repay those notes in fiscal 2026 from operating cash flow and revolver capacity, although the maturity falls in fiscal 2027, and the sources do not show the repayment. Net receivables of USD 312.1 million were sold and derecognised at June 27, 2026 under a programme that was due to expire on September 1, 2026, and supplier-financed payables were USD 23.7 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9, 19, 20, 22, 52, 54; calculation LQ3; calculation A1

The annual figures include Hawthorne in continuing operations while the nine-month and quarterly figures exclude it, so no continuing-operations last-twelve-months series can be built from the filings. This agrees with the source readiness assessment that a continuing-operations series cannot be built; this module therefore uses a consolidated EBITDA that includes discontinued operations, which can be built and is labelled as a different measure. Interim statements are unaudited and seasonal, with more than three quarters of annual sales in the second and third fiscal quarters, so a June balance sheet is not comparable with a September one.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11, 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 5; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against reading the unadjusted 6.12x as overstated is that interest cover on the same basis is only 2.94x and that free cash flow after dividends was USD 15.8 million for nine months, so internal funding for a USD 250.0 million maturity is thin even without the sale loss. The view would change if fiscal 2026 annual results showed earnings below the level implied by the covenant ratios, or if the receivables purchase programme were not renewed; it would improve if the notes were repaid from revolver capacity with liquidity staying well above the USD 277.0 million of debt due within a year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20, 52, 54; calculation F5; calculation V9; calculation LQ3
### Limitations

The credit-agreement Adjusted EBITDA and average total indebtedness are not reconciled, so covenant ratios are quoted as reported and no headroom is calculated. No results after June 27, 2026 are in the sources, the interim figures are unaudited, and no recast full-year FY2025 exists. The maturity schedule is the one printed at September 30, 2025, before the Seventh Amended and Restated Credit Agreement of November 21, 2025 replaced the earlier agreement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 54, 64; 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 136–137

## Gaps

- Adjusted EBITDA as defined in the credit agreement, and average total indebtedness, are not printed in any filing; this restricts covenant leverage and coverage to the ratios the issuer reports, so no headroom can be calculated. Severity High. Obtain the credit agreement or a compliance certificate.

- No recast FY2025 annual statement on the continuing-operations perimeter is supplied, so net sales, gross margin and other lines above EBITDA cannot be put on one perimeter across FY2025 and fiscal 2026. Severity High. Obtain the recast FY2025 or the fiscal 2026 annual report.

- Nothing after the quarter ended June 27, 2026 is in the sources, so net debt, liquidity and the fate of the notes maturing December 15, 2026 are known only to that date. Severity High. Obtain filings after August 5, 2026.

- The filing says the notes due December 15, 2026 will be repaid in fiscal 2026, but that maturity falls in fiscal 2027 under the September 30 fiscal year; which statement is right is not established. Severity Medium. Obtain later filings.

- The only printed maturity ladder is at September 30, 2025 and predates the credit agreement of November 21, 2025, so the ladder and the principal reconciliation are not at the latest balance sheet date. Severity Medium. Obtain a current schedule.
- Quarterly depreciation and amortization is not stated, so EBITDA for the three-month columns is not calculable. Severity Low. Obtain a quarterly cash flow statement.
- Carrying value by instrument, the term loan amortisation schedule and the credit facility spread grid are not disclosed. Severity Low. Obtain the credit agreement.

- The ranking and security of the finance lease obligations of USD 13.1 million are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and the secured and senior subtotals. Severity Low. Obtain lease terms if they matter.

- Cash flows of discontinued operations are not presented separately, so cash-flow figures are consolidated while income statement lines are continuing operations. Severity Low. Operating cash flow of discontinued operations is stated as not material.
- Cells marked as a dash in the statements, such as the loss on sale of business in FY2024, are read as not stated rather than zero. Severity Low. No action.
- Supplier finance obligations at September 30, 2025 are stated only in the Q3 report, not in the FY2025 annual report. Severity Low. No action.
- No quarter ended September 30, 2025 is available as a discrete period, so Q4 FY2025 is not constructed. Severity Low. Obtain the Q4 FY2025 release if needed.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Scotts Miracle-Gro's business is a seasonal branded franchise with two retailers at 52% of sales and about 23% family-partnership ownership, so creditor risk lies in concentration, the Roundup agency and governance transition rather than sponsor leverage.

Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: no extraction is documented and the company prepaid USD 250.0 million and USD 75.0 million of term loan in FY2024 and FY2025, but dividends of USD 116.3 million for nine months continue against thin free cash flow, the incoming chief executive is a general partner of the largest shareholder, and the Hawthorne exit left put and call options with partner-owned vehicles. Board, fee and related-party detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 49, 57, 136; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 12, 39
### Key findings

- Customer concentration and seasonality set the cash profile. The Home Depot and Lowe's together were 52% of FY2025 net sales and 25% of receivables at September 30, 2025, and more than three quarters of North American consumer sales fall in the second and third fiscal quarters, so receivables peak at USD 713.0 million in June and cash needs are financed by the revolver and by selling receivables.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 52

- The Roundup marketing agreement is a material earnings stream that depends on a third party. Net sales associated with it were USD 153.6 million for nine months against USD 134.6 million a year earlier, up 14.12%, for a USD 18.0 million annual contribution, and either party may terminate without a fee if the program's earnings before interest and taxes fall below USD 50.0 million. Those earnings are not printed, but the gross commission of USD 91.8 million in FY2025 is stated to be half of them, which implies about USD 183.6 million, 3.67x the termination floor, so the nearer risk is brand decommissioning or a change of control at Monsanto rather than a shortfall.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 129; calculation R1; calculation R3; calculation R4

- The Hawthorne exit removed a weak segment but left contingent links to partner-owned vehicles. The nine-month loss on sale was USD 101.8 million, USD 35.0 million of cash left with the business, and the non-cash consideration was valued at USD 97.0 million at closing and USD 81.3 million at June 27, 2026; the company consolidates both vehicles and holds options over their assets, so a put exercise would require it to reacquire them against a note. It has also lent to strategic partners and recorded impairments of USD 64.6 million on convertible debt investments in FY2024, so credit losses on such balances are a pattern, not a one-off.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 11, 12, 33; calculation H1; calculation H2

- Control is concentrated and continuous but not sponsor-style. A family partnership holds about 23% of the shares, down from 24% a year earlier, and the chief executive and chairman who led the company since 2001 stepped down in June 2026, with the lead independent director becoming chairman; the successor is a general partner of the same partnership, so influence continues through the transition.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 57; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 39

- Financial policy is dividend-first with a record of debt reduction. The dividend of USD 0.66 a share each quarter has not changed since fiscal 2022 and absorbed 88.04% of nine-month free cash flow, leaving USD 15.8 million, while a USD 500.0 million repurchase authorisation of December 19, 2025 is unused; the credit agreement allows unlimited restricted payments while leverage after the payment is 4.00x or less, otherwise USD 225.0 million a year, and the reported covenant leverage is 3.78x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 58; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20, 21, 23, 51; calculation D2; calculation D3

- Noteholder guarantees are not permanent. The domestic subsidiary guarantees of the senior notes are released in listed circumstances, including designation of a guarantor as an unrestricted subsidiary and release from the credit agreement guarantee at the company's election, so structural support depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 22

- Litigation adds an unquantified claim on cash. Shareholder class and derivative suits allege misstatements about inventories and sales for May 2021 to August 2023, the court partly denied dismissal on April 22, 2026, and no accrual is recorded; asbestos claims are also unaccrued.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 29
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is the repayment record, an independent chair and audited, controls-effective reporting: voluntary term loan prepayments of USD 250.0 million and USD 75.0 million, a lead independent director now chairing the board, and unqualified audit opinions. The rating would rise if the proxy statement shows related-party payments or fees, if the USD 500.0 million repurchase authorisation is used while leverage is above 4.00x, or if a put option over a Hawthorne vehicle is exercised; it would fall if the proxy statement shows an independent board majority and no related-party payments.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee membership, related-party payments and pay are not established, and the Medium governance rating could move either way once they are.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 94
- Customer percentages are printed for FY2025 only, so the 52% concentration is not established for the nine months to June 27, 2026 and may differ in the seasonal peak.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 19
- The option terms of the Hawthorne vehicles, including the partner's identity, are not disclosed beyond the notes, so the contingent funding exposure to the company is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12

- Roundup program earnings are implied from the commission rate rather than printed, so the margin above the termination floor is an inference and the Roundup risk is rated by the agreement's terms, not by a reported cushion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 18
- Nothing after August 5, 2026 is supplied, so the effect of the leadership change, any use of the repurchase authorisation and fiscal 2026 results are not reflected in these findings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 51, 64
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The company issued no new notes in fiscal 2025 or the nine months to June 27, 2026; its only new debt arrangement is the Seventh Amended and Restated Credit Agreement of November 21, 2025, a revolver of USD 1,500.0 million and a term loan of USD 500.0 million maturing November 21, 2030, which replaced the earlier agreement. The transactions that matter are disposals: the Hawthorne business in North America was sold on April 8, 2026 to Vireo for equity securities with an initial fair value of USD 97.0 million after USD 35.0 million of cash was transferred, the Hawthorne business in the Netherlands was sold on September 30, 2025 for USD 8.5 million financed by a seller loan, and the investment holding company that held cannabis-related investments was sold to a partner-owned vehicle on March 14, 2025 for a note of USD 39.0 million. Each sale left the company with a call option, and the vehicles' owner can put the assets back against cancelling the note, so the disposals reduce operating exposure without removing the economic link.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 67, 137; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 11, 12, 19, 20

## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Scotts Miracle-Gro Co (issuer smg-825542), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business, ownership, revenue, cost and cash conversion, credit-translated frameworks, outlook, a qualitative downside scenario and monitoring triggers, drawn from the five supplied filings to the quarter ended 2026-06-27 and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance findings. No rating, legal capacity, recovery value or security recommendation is made.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Scotts Miracle-Gro presents an adequate but leveraged business profile: a branded franchise with improving margins supports cash generation, yet unadjusted leverage of 6.12x, thin free cash flow after dividends and retailer concentration make creditors dependent on revolver access for the December 2026 notes.

The USD 250.0 million of senior notes are due December 15, 2026, 27 days after the as-of date and near the seasonal low in liquidity, which was USD 988.1 million at December 27, 2025 against USD 1,409.5 million at June 27, 2026. Management intends to repay them from operating cash flow and the revolver; whether it has is not established. Free cash flow after dividends over the last twelve months of USD 108.9 million covers only 43.56% of the notes, and reported covenant leverage of 3.78x against a 5.00x maximum is the main reassurance, yet it rests on an earnings definition the filings do not reconcile.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K3; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K26
### Key findings

- The branded franchise is the main credit support, but it is narrow and seasonal. U.S. Consumer produced 91.70% of nine-month net sales, open orders carry over from one year to the next only in small amounts, and 78.3% of annual net sales fall in the second and third fiscal quarters. Net sales rose 2.41% in the nine months to June 27, 2026, from volume and mix of 2.0% and pricing of 0.4%, after falling 3.93% in fiscal 2025 with Hawthorne included, so one spring decides the year's earnings, receivable build and covenant position.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 9, 102; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 40, 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K48

- Retailer concentration caps pricing power and turns the receivable book into a funding risk. The Home Depot and Lowe's were 52% of fiscal 2025 net sales and 25% of receivables, pricing added only 0.4% to nine-month growth and fell 0.1% in the third quarter, and a lost shelf position or a retailer inventory cut would land in the same two quarters that carry most sales and most receivables.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 40; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K47; calculation K49

- Margins have recovered but remain exposed to freight, tariff and commodity costs, and part of the gain is not structural. The gross margin rate rose from 23.94% in FY2024 to 30.59% in FY2025, and was 35.67% over the nine months to June 27, 2026, 1.26 percentage points above the prior-year nine months, helped by mix, Roundup commissions and supply chain savings. The third-quarter rate fell 0.9 percentage points as distribution and warehousing cost rose 10.94%, and over nine months the fall in other selling, general and administrative cost came from lower variable incentive pay, which is likely to reverse when earnings recover.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 22, 102; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 41, 42, 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K15; calculation K16; calculation K17

- Cash conversion is adequate over a full year but leaves little after dividends in the first nine months. Over the last twelve months free cash flow was USD 263.3 million and dividends USD 154.4 million, leaving USD 108.9 million, whereas the nine months to June 27, 2026 left only USD 15.8 million after dividends. The fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 added USD 131.2 million, so the autumn collection of receivables, not the first nine months, funds the dividend, and capital spending of 2.85% of fiscal 2025 net sales is too small to offer much relief. Free cash flow is also flattered by low cash taxes: taxes paid were only USD 5.6 million over nine months against income tax expense of USD 137.8 million on continuing operations, because deferred tax assets are being used, and the filings do not state how long that lasts.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 103, 128; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3, 4, 9, 51; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K9; calculation K24; calculation K50; calculation K51; calculation K58

- Debt service capacity is moderate, not comfortable. Unadjusted debt to EBITDA is 6.12x and EBITDA covers cash interest 2.94x at June 27, 2026, with last-twelve-months earnings absorbing a USD 101.8 million loss on selling Hawthorne; covenant leverage of 3.78x is far lower because the credit agreement uses an adjusted earnings measure. Interest expense fell 15.36% in nine months, but total equity is negative USD 208.7 million and operating lease liabilities of USD 376.8 million, 17.83% of carrying debt, sit outside debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 19, 20, 34, 35, 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K25; calculation K44

- Liquidity is adequate at every fiscal 2026 quarter-end reported, but the notes fall due near the seasonal low and repaying them moves debt toward secured, floating-rate borrowing. Liquidity was USD 988.1 million at December 27, 2025, USD 1,161.8 million at March 28, 2026 and USD 1,409.5 million at June 27, 2026, covering the notes 3.95x, 4.65x and 5.64x. On December 2025 balances, funding the notes wholly from the revolver would leave USD 729.8 million of availability and lift the secured share of principal from 36.46% to 46.30%.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14, 15; 10-Q_2026-03-28_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17, 18; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 19, 20, 54; calculation K4; calculation K26; calculation K27; calculation K28; calculation K29; calculation K30; calculation K36; calculation K37

- Market access looks open, and the maturities that follow this December are spaced. The issuer's reported fair values put the 2029 notes at 97.76% and the 2031 notes at 93.50% of principal on June 27, 2026, consistent with access to capital markets though not dated trading prices. After the December notes the next maturities are the 2029, 2031 and 2032 senior notes, USD 1,350.0 million in all, with the term loan and revolver maturing on November 21, 2030, so the later question is rate and ranking rather than a maturity wall.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 31, 53, 54; calculation K38; calculation K39; calculation K46

- Seasonal funding depends on an uncommitted receivables programme that was due to expire on September 1, 2026, and its renewal is not established. Net receivables derecognised reached USD 654.1 million at March 28, 2026, 87.21% of the USD 750.0 million limit, against USD 312.1 million at June 27, 2026, and recourse is backed by USD 75.0 million of standby letters of credit. Without the programme, liquidity at March 28, 2026 would have been USD 507.7 million rather than USD 1,161.8 million, and USD 257.7 million if the notes had also been funded from the revolver. Business & governance and Financial foundation describe the June 27, 2026 balance sheet as the seasonal peak, but liquidity and funding were tighter at December 27, 2025 and March 28, 2026, so June flatters the cushion and this view uses the earlier quarter-ends.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-28_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 18; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K27; calculation K31; calculation K32; calculation K33

- Governance and financial policy add moderate risk rather than sponsor-style extraction. A family partnership holds about 23% of the shares, the long-serving chief executive stepped down in June 2026 and the successor is a general partner of that partnership, the dividend of USD 0.66 per share each quarter is unchanged since fiscal 2022, the USD 500.0 million repurchase authorisation is unused, and shareholder suits over inventory and sales statements carry no accrual.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 28, 29, 39, 51

- The Hawthorne exit improves the business mix but leaves contingent claims on cash. The business was sold on April 8, 2026 for Vireo shares and a warrant after USD 35.0 million of cash was transferred, with a loss of USD 101.8 million and up to USD 20.0 million of manufacturing services to be supplied at no cost over two years. An ordinary tax loss will reduce cash taxes over several fiscal years, though the amount is not stated, and options held with partner-owned vehicles could require the company to reacquire assets.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12, 27, 39; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious reading is the record of repayment and the room in the structure: the company prepaid USD 250.0 million and USD 75.0 million of term loan in FY2024 and FY2025, carrying debt fell USD 120.4 million between those year-ends, reported covenant leverage is 3.78x against a 5.00x maximum, revolver loans fell from USD 427.0 million at December 27, 2025 to USD 25.0 million at June 27, 2026 as receivables were collected and sold, availability was USD 979.8 million at its lowest fiscal 2026 quarter-end, and the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 produced USD 131.2 million of free cash flow. The view would improve if the notes are repaid without lifting revolver use above its December 2025 level, if the receivables programme is renewed on similar terms and if the gross margin rate holds above the prior-year level. It would worsen if the notes are repaid mainly from revolver borrowings while the programme lapses, if third-quarter freight costs persist, or if dividends keep exceeding free cash flow before the autumn collection.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 103, 136; 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 20, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K9; calculation K45
### Limitations

- The fiscal 2026 annual report and any filing after August 5, 2026 are not supplied, so the conclusion that revolver capacity covers the December 2026 notes rests on the quarter-end balances of the prior year and of fiscal 2026, and could change once actual borrowings, cash and any repayment are known.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 54

- Whether the receivables programme was renewed after September 1, 2026 is not established, so the downside scenario treats a lapse as a sensitivity and the liquidity conclusion improves if renewal on similar terms is confirmed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 52
- Only quarter-end revolver drawings are reported, so the lowest liquidity inside a quarter is not established and the cushion at the seasonal low may be thinner than the quarter-end figures shown.
Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-03-28_smg.htm.jsonl, page 18

- No sector peer or market-share data is supplied, so the view that the business profile is adequate is relative to the issuer's own history and the rating agencies' single-B category ratings, not to other leveraged consumer issuers.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 43
- The credit agreement's adjusted earnings and average indebtedness are not itemised in the filings, so this view gives the reported covenant ratio little weight and states no cushion to the limit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Management gives no quantified outlook and the filings state no leverage target, so the outlook over 12 months to 24 months is the analyst's judgement from reported trends and changes if fiscal 2027 guidance differs.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 56
### Company description and operating model

Scotts Miracle-Gro is the leading marketer of branded consumer lawn and garden products in North America, selling growing media and mulch, lawn care, controls and gardening products under the Scotts, Miracle-Gro, Ortho and Tomcat brands through two operations: U.S. Consumer, 91.70% of nine-month net sales, and Other, mainly Canada, 8.30%. It is also the exclusive agent for Monsanto's consumer Roundup products in the United States, earning commissions, and holds an equity interest in the Bonnie Plants joint venture. Growing media and mulch was 42.27% and lawn care 27.85% of nine-month net sales, so demand follows spring planting and weather. The credit link is that cash flow is visible only from late winter, is concentrated in two quarters and is financed between peaks by the revolver and the sale of receivables, so the franchise supports debt service in a normal season but gives creditors little warning of a bad one.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 5, 8, 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 38, 43, 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K12; calculation K54; calculation K55
### Ownership and group structure

Scotts Miracle-Gro is a listed company with no sponsor; a family partnership holds about 23% of the shares, down from 24% a year earlier, and the incoming chief executive, in office from June 26, 2026, is a general partner of that partnership. Substantially all domestic subsidiaries guarantee the credit facilities and the senior notes, but the note guarantees can be released, including when a guarantor is designated an unrestricted subsidiary, so structural support depends on indenture terms that are not supplied. Hawthorne North America was sold on April 8, 2026 for Vireo shares and a warrant, which the company transferred to a consolidated partner-owned vehicle for a promissory note, and an earlier sale of an investment holding company went to a second such vehicle; the company holds call options and the vehicles can put assets back. The credit consequence is that owner behaviour is more predictable than under a sponsor, with no extraction through fees or leveraged recapitalisation seen in the filings, but the dividend of USD 0.66 per share each quarter keeps priority over faster debt paydown.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 49, 57, 81; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12, 22, 23, 39, 56
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is recurring in category but not contractual: consumers replenish lawn and garden products each season, yet retailers place orders from late winter and the company reports minimal carryover of open orders, so there is no backlog to underwrite the year. Net sales fell 3.93% in fiscal 2025 with Hawthorne included and rose 2.41% in nine months to June 27, 2026 without it, from volume and mix of 2.0% and pricing of 0.4%, with a favourable mix from branded soils, grass seed, controls and fertiliser offsetting lower mulch sales. Pricing power is limited: two retailers hold 52% of sales, the company states that market conditions may limit its ability to raise prices to offset raw material costs, and private label competes in its markets. The credit implication is that cost inflation is absorbed in margin before it is recovered in price, and that demand is discretionary and exposed to weather and consumer behaviour.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 9, 19, 102; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 40, 41; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K48; calculation K49
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Materials were 50.98% of nine-month cost of sales, manufacturing labor and overhead 23.97% and distribution and warehousing 21.20%, so most cost is variable with volume or input prices rather than fixed. Inputs include urea and other fertiliser, resin, diesel, natural gas, peat, bark and grass seed; the company buys part of its needs ahead of the season and hedges diesel and urea, but imports from China and other countries expose it to tariffs. Selling cost carries operating leverage: advertising and other marketing were USD 196.8 million over nine months, 43.67% of selling, general and administrative cost, after planned increases. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through marketing and incentive pay, but not against a sustained freight or tariff shock, as the 0.9 percentage point fall in the third-quarter gross margin rate shows.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 19, 22, 90; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 43; calculation K16; calculation K17; calculation K18; calculation K19; calculation K20; calculation K21; calculation K22
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending was USD 97.4 million in fiscal 2025, 2.85% of net sales and 1.30x depreciation and amortization, so the business needs modest reinvestment but cannot cut it enough to matter against USD 154.4 million of dividends over twelve months. The main cash swing is working capital: inventory is built in the first quarter, USD 846.7 million at December 27, 2025 against USD 481.4 million at June 27, 2026, and receivables rose USD 552.1 million over the nine months to June 27, 2026 and are collected in the fourth quarter, which is why free cash flow was USD 132.1 million for nine months but USD 263.3 million over twelve months. Cash interest paid was USD 117.4 million over twelve months, while cash taxes paid were only USD 5.6 million over nine months, a benefit from deferred tax assets that the Hawthorne tax loss extends by an amount not stated and that will not last indefinitely. EBITDA therefore converted into free cash flow of 64.37% in fiscal 2025, adequate for debt service but with limited surplus for deleveraging once dividends are paid. Supplier-financed payables of USD 23.7 million at June 27, 2026 are small beside the receivables programme, so that funding source adds little risk.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 103, 118, 128; 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3, 4, 9, 27, 51, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K2; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K23; calculation K24; calculation K50; calculation K52; calculation K53; calculation K56; calculation K58; calculation K59
### Credit-translated frameworks

Competitive rivalry is moderate and mostly brand against private label: the company competes with Spectrum Brands, Central Garden & Pet, Kellogg Garden Products, Oldcastle Retail and regional makers on brand, advertising and retailer relationships, so advertising of USD 148.9 million over nine months, up 15.5%, has to be sustained to protect share and keeps selling cost semi-fixed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation K21; calculation K57

Buyer power is high and is the weakest force for creditors: two retailers took 52% of fiscal 2025 net sales and the receivables the company sells come from five specified customers, so a delisting, inventory cut or change in terms would hit sales, receivables funding and bargaining position together.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation K49

Supplier power is moderate: the company relies on a limited base of suppliers and on commodities whose prices it cannot control, but it hedges diesel and urea and states that sufficient raw materials were available in fiscal 2025, so the exposure is cost volatility more than supply loss.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 22

The threat of new entrants and substitutes is limited for national branded products by brand trademarks, retailer relationships and product registration, but private label and other named competitors such as Sunday Lawn Care cap pricing and are the main route by which share could erode.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 9, 10

Political and regulatory factors matter through tariffs on goods imported from China and elsewhere, and through pesticide and fertiliser rules that can restrict ingredients or ban product categories; economic factors matter through elevated interest rates, inflationary pressure on input costs and consumer behaviour, which the company says it monitors. Social and climate factors act through weather, which makes the effect of abnormal seasons hard to predict. Technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the filings read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 22, 24, 62; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 39

- Credit strengths are the leading brands and exclusive Roundup agency, a gross margin rate of 35.67% over nine months, a revolver commitment of USD 1,500.0 million with availability of at least USD 979.8 million at each fiscal 2026 quarter-end reported, and a record of term loan prepayment.
Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 40, 54; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K15; calculation K26

- Credit weaknesses are retailer concentration, earnings that depend on one spring, negative equity of USD 208.7 million, unadjusted leverage of 6.12x and dividends that absorb 58.64% of last-twelve-months free cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K8; calculation K49

- Opportunities that could raise credit quality are repayment of the notes without added revolver use, lower interest cost as the term loan is paid down, cash tax savings from the Hawthorne loss and continued mix toward branded products.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 39, 41; calculation K25

- Threats that could lower credit quality are tariffs and freight, a lapsed receivables programme, a poor spring, loss of Roundup brand support at the third-party owner, and shareholder suits that carry no accrual.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 29, 43, 52; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 months to 24 months the main events are the repayment of the senior notes due December 15, 2026, the fate of the receivables programme after September 1, 2026, the spring 2027 season under a new chief executive and the first full year without Hawthorne. Tailwinds are interest expense down 15.36% in nine months, the Hawthorne tax loss that will extend low cash taxes over several years, continued Roundup agreement income and a mix toward branded products. Headwinds are distribution cost, a rise in cash taxes once deferred tax assets are used, tariffs, elevated interest rates and consumer behaviour, the last three named by the company as conditions it monitors. Interest rate swaps hedge at most USD 450.0 million of the USD 512.5 million of variable-rate debt, USD 300.0 million of which expires by April 7, 2027, leaving at most USD 250.0 million, 51.28% of the term loan, hedged afterwards, so interest cost becomes more sensitive to rates in the 2027 season.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 27, 39, 41, 43, 55, 56; calculation K25; calculation K40; calculation K41; calculation K42; calculation K43

Over three years to five years the sequence is the 2029 notes of USD 450.0 million, the credit agreement in November 2030, then the 2031 and 2032 notes, and the filings state no leverage target. Medium-term credit quality therefore depends on whether the margin gain holds, whether the dividend stays covered by free cash flow and whether debt is paid down in the autumn collection period each year. The company expects weather in any one year not to change longer-term category growth, which supports demand, but climate change is named as a risk to the availability and cost of inputs and to consumer behaviour.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 61; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 53, 54
### Qualitative downside scenario

The realistic downside is a weak spring 2027 season, from cool and wet weather or a retailer inventory reduction with freight and tariff costs still high, that coincides with a lapsed receivables programme and the December 2026 notes. The first operational break would show in the second fiscal quarter, which with the third carries 78.3% of annual net sales: shipments fall short while manufacturing labor and overhead of USD 459.9 million over nine months and planned advertising of USD 148.9 million do not flex in season. The gross margin rate, which fell 0.9 percentage points in the latest quarter with distribution cost up 10.94%, would fall further and EBITDA would fall faster than sales.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 19, 24; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 41, 43; calculation K10; calculation K16; calculation K17

The financial transmission runs through working capital and starts with the revolver. The notes fall due at the seasonal low: on December 27, 2025 balances, liquidity of USD 988.1 million would fall to USD 517.8 million if the programme were not available and the revolver also funded the notes. The spring build then adds receivables and inventory: at March 28, 2026 the programme had removed USD 654.1 million of receivables, and without it and after funding the notes liquidity would have been USD 257.7 million, 22.18% of the reported USD 1,161.8 million, before any earnings shortfall. Leverage then rises from both sides, lower EBITDA and higher revolver debt, moving the reported covenant ratio from 3.78x toward its 5.00x maximum on a definition that cannot be tested here. This is arithmetic on reported balances, not a forecast.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 15; 10-Q_2026-03-28_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 18; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation K26; calculation K27; calculation K32; calculation K33; calculation K34; calculation K35

Management levers are advertising and other marketing of USD 196.8 million over nine months after planned increases, variable incentive pay, capital spending of USD 63.1 million, the unused USD 500.0 million repurchase authorisation and the dividend of USD 116.3 million for nine months. On these figures resilience appears sufficient for one weak season only if the receivables programme or a substitute stays available; if it lapses and the notes are repaid from the revolver, liquidity at the spring peak would be thin and a dividend cut would become the main lever, with market access for the 2029 notes the next test. This is the analyst's judgement. The observable triggers are the status of the receivables programme, revolver loans at the next two quarter-ends, retailer order commentary in spring 2027 and the reported covenant leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 43, 51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K21; calculation K33; calculation K50
### Overall credit view

Overall, Scotts Miracle-Gro presents an adequate business profile supported by leading brands, a nine-month gross margin rate of 35.67%, up 1.26 percentage points on the prior-year nine months, and a USD 1,500.0 million revolver with availability of at least USD 979.8 million at each fiscal 2026 quarter-end reported, but credit quality is constrained by retailer concentration, a two-quarter earnings season, thin free cash flow after dividends in the first nine months and negative equity. Cash-flow durability appears adequate over a full year, with USD 108.9 million left after dividends over the last twelve months, and weak before the autumn collection. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on revolver availability, the receivables programme and the covenant earnings measure for the 2026 notes, and on market access for the 2029 notes. The primary downside path is a weak spring season with a lapsed receivables programme, which raises revolver use and leverage together. Comparison with sector peers is not established because no peer data is supplied; both rating agencies kept ratings in the single-B category in August 2025. Further analysis would require the fiscal 2026 annual report, the renewal status of the receivables programme, the credit agreement's earnings definition and the proxy statement. The top risk is dependence on revolver capacity and the receivables programme for the spring peak and the December 2026 maturity.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-03-28_smg.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 52, 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K6; calculation K26
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest support is the franchise. Leading brands and the exclusive Roundup agency produced a gross margin rate of 35.67% over nine months, up 1.26 percentage points, which lifts EBITDA and interest cover and lets the company absorb moderate cost increases. The second support is liquidity: availability under the USD 1,500.0 million revolver was USD 979.8 million at the lowest fiscal 2026 quarter-end reported and USD 1,381.8 million at June 27, 2026, so liquidity covered the USD 250.0 million of notes 3.95x at the low and 5.64x in June. The third is a record of paying debt down, with carrying debt falling USD 120.4 million between FY2024 and FY2025 and a lower interest bill, which gives creditors evidence that cash is applied to debt in good years.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 103; 10-Q_2025-12-27_smg.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_smg.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 40, 54; calculation K4; calculation K15; calculation K28; calculation K45

The largest weakness is the funding of the seasonal build. The programme that removed USD 654.1 million of receivables at March 28, 2026 is uncommitted, and without it liquidity at that date would have been USD 507.7 million rather than USD 1,161.8 million. The second is thin cash after dividends, USD 15.8 million for nine months and USD 108.9 million for twelve months, which leaves little internal funding for the notes. The third is retailer concentration, 52% of fiscal 2025 net sales in two customers, which limits pricing and concentrates risk in the two quarters that earn most of the year. Unadjusted leverage of 6.12x, negative equity, cost exposure to freight and tariffs, and free cash flow that benefits from cash taxes of only USD 5.6 million over nine months complete the weaknesses.
